statement: The model-independent quotient (F18) — Let $X$ and $Y$ be proper, regular, integral finite-type $K$-schemes with function field $L$. Their finite \emph{\'etale} extensions of $L$ form the same full subcategory of finite separable $L$-algebras. Consequently their quotients $G_L\twoheadrightarrow\pi_1(X)$ and $G_L\twoheadrightarrow\pi_1(Y)$ have the same kernel, with the generic geometric point fixed. The assertion also holds in positive characteristic whenever these proper regular models exist.

statement: Riemann--Zariski points and the noetherian correction (F21) — The inverse limit of all proper integral $K$-models of $L$, with its colimit local rings, has points exactly the valuation rings $V$ of $L$ containing $K$. This identification uses no resolution of singularities. Its noetherian local rings are exactly $L$ and the discrete valuation rings of $L/K$. A discrete valuation ring need not be divisorial: there exists one for $\mathbb Q(x,y)/\mathbb Q$ with residue field $\mathbb Q$ and hence manuscript codimension two.

statement: Explicit valuations with divisible value groups — For $K$ of characteristic zero and $L=K(x,y)$, the following valuations trivial on $K$ exist: \[ (\Gamma_v,\kappa(v))=(\mathbb Q,K),\qquad (\Gamma_v,\kappa(v))=(\mathbb Z[1/2],K). \] They have centers on the boundary of $(\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})^2$, and their centers can lie on only one boundary component. This construction will supply the corrections to F19, F20, F22 and F25.

statement: Inertia, its ranks, and a splitting (F22) — For every valuation $v$ of $L/K$ there are a continuous exact sequence and a canonical pairing \[ 1\longrightarrow I_v\longrightarrow D_v\longrightarrow G_{\kappa(v)}\longrightarrow1, \qquad I_v\simeq\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(\Gamma_v\otimes\mathbb Q/\Gamma_v,\mu_\infty\bigr) \simeq\operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma_v,T). \] The sequence has a continuous splitting, with no canonical choice. The conjugation action on inertia is the cyclotomic action on the values in $T$. More precisely, \[ I_v\simeq\prod_{\ell}\mathbb Z_\ell(1)^{r_\ell},\qquad r_\ell=\dim_{\mathbb F_\ell}(\Gamma_v/\ell\Gamma_v) \le\dim_{\mathbb Q}(\Gamma_v\otimes\mathbb Q) \le\operatorname{trdeg}_K L-\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(v). \] The product decomposition is noncanonical. Neither the manuscript codimension nor, in general, the rational rank determines the inertia group. In particular $\Gamma_v=\mathbb Q$ gives $I_v=1$, and $\Gamma_v=\mathbb Z[1/2]$ gives $I_v=\prod_{\ell\ne2}\mathbb Z_\ell(1)$.

statement: The exact inertia normalizer for arbitrary valuations (F19) — Let $I_v\ne1$. Let $\Delta_v$ be the largest divisible convex subgroup of the ordered group $\Gamma_v$, and let $w$ be the coarsening with value group $\Gamma_v/\Delta_v$, with its prolongation induced by $\overline v$. Then \[ I_w=I_v,\qquad N_{G_L}(I_v)=D_w, \qquad N_{P_{L/K}}(I_v)=D_w\cap P_{L/K}. \] There is an exact sequence \[ 1\longrightarrow I_v\longrightarrow N_{P_{L/K}}(I_v) \longrightarrow G_{\kappa(w)\overline K}\longrightarrow1. \] Here $\kappa(w)\overline K$ is the compositum inside the residue algebraic closure induced by $\overline v$. Consequently geometric self-normalization holds precisely when that compositum is separably closed. The arithmetic identity $N_{G_L}(I_v)=D_v$ holds precisely when the induced residual valuation $v/w$ is henselian on $\kappa(w)$. It holds in particular for every rank-one valuation with nontrivial inertia, including every DVR. For $I_v=1$ the inertia normalizer is all of $G_L$.

The arithmetic assertion $N_{G_L}(I_v)=D_v$ is false for general valuations with $I_v\ne1$, already for $L=\mathbb Q(x,y,z)$. D5 is the exact replacement.

statement: Detecting a center: the DVR assertion and its arbitrary-valuation extension (F20) — For a DVR $V$ of $L/K$ and an elementary tower $U/K$ of smooth curves with good relative compactifications and no fiber of type $(0,0)$ or $(0,1)$, the homomorphism $I_v\to\pi_1(U)$ is trivial precisely when $V$ has a center on $U$. For an arbitrary valuation, having a center still implies that this homomorphism is trivial, but its converse is false even for $U=(\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})^2$. Outside the indicated curve-type hypothesis the converse fails already for $\mathbb A^1$ and a DVR.

statement: Restriction of valuation rings and of local Galois groups (F23) — Let $K\subset L_1\subset L$ and $V_1=V\cap L_1$. Then $V_1$ is a valuation ring with fraction field $L_1$, and reduction embeds $\kappa(V_1)$ into $\kappa(V)$. With compatible algebraic closures and prolongations, restriction gives continuous homomorphisms \[ D_V\longrightarrow D_{V_1},\qquad I_V\longrightarrow I_{V_1}. \] Their existence does not assert that either homomorphism is injective or surjective. If $L_1/K$ has transcendence degree one and $\kappa(V)$ is algebraic over $K$, $V_1$ is the DVR of a closed point on the proper smooth curve with function field $L_1$.

statement: The written function-field formula at scan 127 (F24) — Assume here that $K$ is finitely generated over $\mathbb Q$. The two assertions (32)--(33) with subscript $L$ have the same truth value, but their common assertion of triviality is false. For $L=\mathbb Q(t)$, the $t$-adic place, and a decomposition section $s:G_{\mathbb Q}\to D_v\subset G_L$, both fixed groups are $I_v=T\ne1$. Under the quotient to $\pi_1(U)$ for $U=\mathbb P^1\setminus\{1,2,\infty\}$, this section becomes the point section at $0$ and both fixed groups become trivial. For point sections of elementary anabelian $U$ the corresponding $U$-formulas hold.

statement: Normalizers of decomposition groups (completion of F19) — Put $H=L_v^h$. If $\kappa(v)$ is not separably closed, then \[ N_{G_L}(D_v)=D_v. \] If $\kappa(v)$ is separably closed, then $D_v=I_v$; its normalizer is $D_w$ as in D5 when $I_v\ne1$, and is $G_L$ when $I_v=1$. In all cases $N_{P_{L/K}}(D_v)=N_{G_L}(D_v)\cap P_{L/K}$. For the geometric decomposition subgroup $D_v^{\mathrm{geom}}=D_v\cap P_{L/K}$, the same alternatives hold with $G_L,L,\kappa(v)$ replaced by $P_{L/K},L\overline K,\kappa(v)\overline K$: it is self-normalizing when this last residue field is not separably closed; otherwise it equals $I_v$ and D5 gives its normalizer.

statement: The local group and the two local injectivity assertions (F25, 1$^\circ$) — For the strict henselization $R=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ there is a parameter-labelled isomorphism \[ \pi_1\bigl(\operatorname{Spec}R[1/(z_1\cdots z_r)]\bigr)=T^r. \] Its $i$th factor is the meridian of $D_i$, characterized by its action on compatible roots of $z_i$. For an ordinary point $x$, the henselian local group fits into \[ 1\longrightarrow T^r\longrightarrow \pi_1\bigl(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}^{h}\cap U\bigr) \longrightarrow G_{\kappa(x)}\longrightarrow1. \] When $\kappa(x)/K$ is finite, injectivity of the entire local homomorphism into $\pi_1(U)$ is equivalent to injectivity of its restriction to $T^r$. This equivalence does not hold for general nonclosed points. If $U$ is a hyperbolic elementary polycurve, each individual branch meridian $T\to\pi_1(U)$ is injective, so the geometric local homomorphism is injective whenever $r=1$.

statement: The blow-up map, and the product compactification (F25, 1$^\circ$) — For $U=(\mathbb P^1\setminus\{0,1,\infty\})^2$, blow up $(0,2)$ in $(\mathbb P^1)^2$. At the intersection of the exceptional divisor with the strict transform of $x=0$, the local homomorphism is \[ T^2\longrightarrow T\hookrightarrow\pi_1(U),\qquad (a,b)\longmapsto a+b. \] Its kernel is $\{(a,-a):a\in T\}$. Thus 1$^\circ$ is false even for an elementary hyperbolic surface. On the original product compactification of any two smooth hyperbolic curves, every geometric local meridian homomorphism is injective. That product compactification is terminal among smooth proper compactifications of the same $U$ with simple normal crossings boundary: every such compactification has a unique morphism to it inducing the identity on $U$.

statement: The image of an arbitrary valuation at a crossing (F25, 2$^\circ$) — Let a valuation $v$ have center $x$ on $X$, let the branches through $x$ have parameters $z_1,\ldots,z_r$, and put $\gamma_i=v(z_i)$. The homomorphism from valuation inertia to the local geometric group is \[ \rho_v:\operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma_v,T)\longrightarrow T^r, \qquad \chi\longmapsto(\chi(\gamma_1),\ldots,\chi(\gamma_r)). \] It is dual to the homomorphism of discrete torsion groups \[ \psi_v:\mathbb Q^r/\mathbb Z^r\longrightarrow (\Gamma_v\otimes\mathbb Q)/\Gamma_v, \qquad (q_i)\longmapsto\sum_iq_i\gamma_i\pmod{\Gamma_v}. \] Consequently $\operatorname{im}\rho_v$ is open exactly when $\ker\psi_v$ is finite, and it is all of $T^r$ exactly when $\ker\psi_v=0$. More explicitly, openness requires rational independence of the $\gamma_i$. Under that independence, with $\Lambda=\sum_i\mathbb Z\gamma_i$, \[ \ker\psi_v=(\Gamma_v\cap\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q}\{\gamma_i\})/\Lambda. \] Thus openness is exactly finite saturation index, and surjectivity is exactly equality of this saturation with $\Lambda$. Equality of rational rank and number of branches alone is insufficient.

statement: The precise criterion for the stratum extension (F26) — Work first over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. For a nonempty connected open stratum \[ S=D_J^\circ=\Bigl(\bigcap_{j\in J}D_j\Bigr)\setminus\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\notin J}D_i\Bigr), \qquad L_j=N_{D_j/X}|_S, \] let $P=\prod_{j\in J,S}L_j^\times$ be the product of the punctured normal line bundles. Its fundamental groups have the exact homotopy sequence \[ \pi_2^{\mathrm{et}}(S)\xrightarrow{\partial}T^J \longrightarrow\pi_1(P)\longrightarrow\pi_1(S)\longrightarrow1. \] The same sequence computes the punctured tubular neighborhood of this stratum. With positive fiber meridians and the clutching convention specified below, \[ \partial(a)=\bigl(\langle c_1(L_j),a\rangle\bigr)_{j\in J}. \] In particular (37) is left exact precisely when these Chern evaluations vanish. An equivalent criterion, involving only finite covers and line bundles, is: for every positive integer $n$ there is a connected finite \emph{\'etale} cover $S'\to S$ such that every $L_j|_{S'}$ is an $n$th tensor power in $\operatorname{Pic}(S')$. Vanishing of $\pi_2^{\mathrm{et}}(S)$ suffices, but is not necessary. Over a nonclosed field the same assertion descends with the cyclotomic action and the permutation of geometric branch labels.

statement: Algebraic residues need not be finite; the arithmetic openness criterion — A valuation of a finitely generated extension $L/K$ can have residue field algebraic and infinite over $K$, even when it is a DVR. For a valuation with algebraic residue field centered at $x$ on $X$, the entire homomorphism $D_v\to\pi_1(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}^h\cap U)$ has open image precisely when both $[\kappa(v):\kappa(x)]$ and $|\ker\psi_v|$ of E3 are finite. Its image is the entire local group precisely when $\kappa(v)=\kappa(x)$ and $\ker\psi_v=0$. Thus the inserted ``fini'' on scans 124 and 130 is an additional hypothesis, not a consequence of algebraicity.

statement: A simply connected scheme as a fiber functor — Let $Y$ be connected and locally noetherian, and let $Z\to Y$ be nonempty and connected with trivial \emph{\'etale} fundamental group. Then \[ F_Z:\operatorname{FEt}(Y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{FinSets},\qquad E\longmapsto\pi_0(E\times_Y Z) \] is a fiber functor. A map of such pointed data gives a genuine continuous homomorphism of its automorphism groups. For a morphism $f:X\to Y$, the relative kernel depends on the choice of connecting path through conjugation by $\pi_1(X)$; that action need not be inner as an action on the kernel itself.

statement: Relative kernels, universal covers, and the missing left exactness — For connected locally noetherian pointed schemes $f:X\to Y$, put $H=\operatorname{im}(\pi_1(X)\to\pi_1(Y))$. The pointed connected pro-finite-\emph{\'etale} cover $Y_H\to Y$ corresponding to $H$ admits a unique pointed lift of $f$, the map $\pi_1(X)\to\pi_1(Y_H)=H$ is surjective, and its kernel is unchanged. Pullback of the universal pro-cover of $Y_H$ has fundamental group that kernel. The identification of this kernel with a geometric fiber group additionally requires injectivity of the fiber homomorphism; an exact homotopy sequence beginning only at that fiber group does not supply it.

statement: Recovering the model quotient and the function field — For a regular integral finite-type model $U$ of $L/K$, the kernel of $G_L\to\pi_1(U)$ is the closed normal subgroup generated by the inertia groups of its codimension-one local rings. It is equally generated by the inertia groups of all valuations with a center on $U$. For the nonempty open subschemes of one fixed normal model, \[ G_L\simeq\varprojlim_U\pi_1(U),\qquad P_{L/K}\simeq\varprojlim_U\pi_1(U_{\overline K}) \] when the models are geometrically connected; in general the second formula uses the kernels of the maps to $G_K$. For $U=X\setminus Z$ with $X$ proper regular, the kernel of $\pi_1(U)\to\pi_1(X)$ is generated by the boundary-divisor inertia images.

statement: Model opens, finite unions, and when the Riemann--Zariski space is a scheme — The points of manuscript codimension one are exactly the divisorial valuation rings, as asserted on scans 121--122. The Riemann--Zariski space is the proper normal curve for transcendence degree one, a point for degree zero, and has no nonempty affine open in its locally ringed-space structure for transcendence degree at least two. The claim on scan 123 that the opens supplied by models are not stable under finite unions is false: these opens are precisely the quasicompact opens, and they are stable under finite unions and finite intersections.

statement: What the boundary incidence complex does describe — For a smooth complex variety, the incidence complex of a simple normal crossings boundary has the same connected components as the boundary. It must have a cell for every connected component of each intersection, not merely one simplex for each nonempty set of labels. It does not in general give the homotopy type of a punctured neighborhood, even when all its strata are points. The pro-system of complements of compact subsets of $U(\mathbb C)$ is independent of its smooth proper compactification; punctured boundary neighborhoods are a cofinal system in it.

statement: Conjugacy along strata and the arithmetic stabilizer — On a geometrically connected open stratum with labelled geometric boundary branches, its homomorphisms $T^J\to\pi_1(U_{\overline K})$ are conjugate by geometric paths. Arithmetic transport acts on the labels by permutation and on each $T$ by the cyclotomic character. An individual geometric branch carries canonical equivariance under its Galois stabilizer; the full Galois group preserves the orbit of branches, and invariance of an individual image can fail. Thus scan 136's full-group assertion needs geometric connectedness or this stabilizer correction.
